data.title: Dioscorea polystachya Turcz. attenuates male reproductive aging through modulation of mTOR-Beclin-1-mediated autophagy in Leydig and Sertoli cells
data.authors: Zhang Y; Feng J; Xie T; Zhang X; Pan D; Liu S; Zhao D; Wang S; Liu M; Yu S

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Rat (aged model); Mouse Leydig (TM3) and Sertoli (TM4) cells
data.finding: Chinese yam protein extract (CYCSE) attenuates male reproductive aging by activating testicular autophagy through the mTOR-Beclin-1 axis in Leydig and Sertoli cells; mTOR activation blocks protective effects.
data.abstract_excerpt: This study investigated the efficacy of Chinese yam protein extract (CYCSE) from Dioscorea polystachya in attenuating aging-related reproductive decline. In aged rats and D-galactose-induced senescent mouse Leydig and Sertoli cells, CYCSE ameliorated testicular histopathology, restored sperm parameters, increased testosterone levels, reduced senescence markers (SA-beta-gal, p16, p21, p53), and mitigated oxidative stress. TEM confirmed restored autophagic flux in senescent cells. Mechanistically, CYCSE restored autophagic activity via the mTOR-Beclin-1 signaling axis.

extracted_findings.intervention: Chinese yam protein extract (CYCSE); mTOR activator (control)
extracted_findings.effect: CYCSE suppresses mTOR to activate autophagy via Beclin-1, reducing senescence markers and restoring reproductive function in aged testicular cells
